claims.text: Adding approximately 5 at% Hf to nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 will suppress Cr–V-rich precipitate formation near 8 dpa.
The Hf-modified alloy will retain the low irradiation hardening and radiation resistance of W38Ta36Cr15V11.
The Hf-modified alloy will remain practical for bulk manufacture.
The baseline W38Ta36Cr15V11 material was produced by magnetron sputtering.
The baseline material has a bimodal grain-size distribution, with most grains no larger than 100 nm.
The baseline W38Ta36Cr15V11 material has a single-phase BCC structure.
Cr and V segregate to grain boundaries and triple junctions in the baseline alloy.
The baseline alloy develops approximately 3–5 nm Cr–V-rich precipitates after irradiation to about 8 dpa.
A proposed modified composition is approximately W38Ta31Cr10V11Hf5.
Approximately 5 at% Hf will improve solid-solution stability and inhibit Cr and V segregation.
Irradiation of W38Ta36Cr15V11 has previously been performed at 1073 K up to 8 dpa.
A temperature near 1073 K is representative of fusion first-wall or divertor operation.
Hf will modify grain-boundary and matrix chemistry, reducing Cr and V mobility and segregation.
Hf has a high melting temperature and a substantial size mismatch with the host lattice.
Hf-induced lattice distortion and solute interactions will impede Cr/V diffusion and point-defect mobility, thereby inhibiting radiation-induced segregation and precipitation.
The baseline alloy exhibits no irradiation-created dislocation loops at 8 dpa and nearly negligible irradiation hardening.
The precipitate-suppression benefit of Hf is expected to persist up to approximately 8–10 dpa near 1073 K.
There is uncertainty about the Hf concentration that would suppress precipitation without causing other phase instabilities or processing complications.

contradictions.description: The nominal modified formula W38Ta31Cr10V11Hf5 totals only 95 at%, not approximately 100 at%. It also reduces both Ta and Cr, whereas the text describes Hf as partially substituting Cr or simply being added.
The hypothesis claims practical bulk manufacturability, but the proposed specimens are magnetron-sputtered films and the listed characterization does not directly test bulk fabrication feasibility.
